title: schema-validation: streaming-safe response_format with strict error mode and OpenAI-compat fallbacks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customers want first-class JSON Schema-backed structured outputs that behave predictably in both streaming and non-streaming modes and interoperate with OpenAI-style response_format and function-calling expectations. This PR implements a server-side JSON Schema validation pipeline for response_format/schema, a configurable strict mode that returns structured validation errors, streaming-safe schema enforcement with graceful fallback, and compatibility hooks for the OpenAI compatibility layer. Changes are intended to be conservative: defaults preserve existing behavior; strict mode must be opted into via request params or headers.

Summary of changes:
- New response_format validation component wired into the request handler that validates model outputs against provided JSON Schemas (supports draft-07 and Draft 2019-09 subset used by common tooling).
- "strict" behavior: when enabled (x-redwood-strict-schema: true or response_format.mode=strict), the platform will reject or mark responses with structured error payloads on schema violations. The error payload follows a stable shape (error_type, path, message, suggestion) to be consumed by SDKs and client code.
- Streaming behavior: for streaming requests we perform incremental schema checks on partial JSON fragments and emit structured validation frames as part of the stream when irrecoverable violations are detected. To avoid noisy false positives we:
  * attempt incremental parse/recovery for common streaming patterns (chunked arrays, partial objects)
  * delay hard strict failures until a complete top-level object is assembled where possible
  * provide a per-request fallback policy (response_format.streaming_fallback=non_strict | strict_delayed | fail_immediate)
- OpenAI compatibility: the openai-compat layer now maps response_format to the OpenAI "response_format"/"function_call" semantics and ensures SDKs receive the same error shapes.
Function/tool-calling: if a schema is attached to a function return type, we validate the returned object before emitting a tool call to the client; in strict mode the tool call is blocked and a structured error is returned so callers can retry with corrected prompts.
- Error telemetry and observability: new metrics (schema.validation.total, schema.validation.failures, schema.validation.streaming_incidents) and traces for validation latency.
Docs: added migration notes and examples for Python/TS SDKs.
Backwards compatibility: default (no strict header/param) keeps previous permissive acceptance; streaming messages are unchanged by default except extra validation frame types when enabled.

Risk and mitigation: incremental parser improvements could surface edge-case regressions for badly-minted model output; mitigations include conservative delay of failures in streaming mode, feature flags for rollout, and a canary rollout to Dedicated clusters.

Checklist:
- [x] server-side validator and incremental parser
- [x] streaming integration and new frame types
- [x] openai-compat mappings and SDK examples
- [x] unit + integration tests + e2e against representative models
- [x] docs and migration guidance
- [x] added metrics and tracing
